question: Using determinants, obtain the equation of the line passing through $(-1,2)$ and $(2,-4)$. Hence, verify whether $(3,-6)$ lies on this line.
explanation:
Determinant condition for the line
Let $(x,y)$ be an arbitrary point on the required line. Then, $$\begin{vmatrix}x&y&1\\-1&2&1\\2&-4&1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
Expansion of the determinant
Expanding along the first row gives $$x(2+4)-y(-1-2)+[4-4]=0$$ Therefore, $$6x+3y=0$$
Equation of the line
Dividing by $3$, the required equation is $$2x+y=0$$
Verification of the given point
For $(3,-6)$, $$2(3)+(-6)=0$$ Hence, $(3,-6)$ satisfies the equation and lies on the line.

options.A: $2x-y=0$; $(3,-6)$ does not lie on the line.
options.C: $2x+y=0$; $(3,-6)$ does not lie on the line.
